thread:
emma (AE): Heads-up — Skyline (fintech) wants a firm commit for Q3. They expect 650 rps peak for their transformer chat model, 18k tokens/session avg. Asking about reserved GPU sizing + burst credits. Any red flags?

mike (Sales Eng): 650 rps peak, 18k tokens — that's nontrivial. Do they expect sustained 650 or short spikes?

emma (AE): They said sustained during market open (90m window), and spikes outside that. Wants predictable latency under 300ms p50 for chat.

julia (Solutions): Key questions: are they fine with quantized model variants? That cuts GPU footprint ~2.5x. Also need KV-cache warmup plan — long prompts mean big KV state.

rohan (SRE): For 650 rps sustained at ~18k tokens, rough compute estimate: assuming our optimized runtime on A100-ish equiv, about 0.12 tokens/ms per GPU? ballpark. We should convert to GPU-seconds. I can do a quick back-of-envelope later.

noah (Infra): Also need to know if Skyline wants Private (VPC) or Dedicated hosted. Private adds AZ spread and we can't burst into hosted pool. Licensing for on-prem can affect lead time.

emma (AE): They want Dedicated with a Private control plane (enterprise). Security Q already flagged KMS + SOC2 questions. We have their questionnaire but postponed sizing until we confirm preheat/autoscale plan.

mike (Sales Eng): Pricing question from procurement: if we recommend 6 reserved GPUs + burst credits, how do we model cost vs fully reserved for the 90m window? They want a monthly number + worst-case overage.

julia (Solutions): Suggested plan: 4 reserved GPUs for baseline + 2 burst GPUs (prewarm on schedule). Autoscale policy: can scale to 8 for 15min bursts using burst credits. Also enable prefix-KV caching and inter-request batcher tuned for small latencies.

emma (AE): Skyline asked for an ops runbook in handover — preheat cron, canary rollout steps, and fallback to smaller model if latencies spike.

rohan (SRE): Draft autoscale snippet (ops config):
```
autoscale_policy: 
  min_replicas: 4
  reserved_replicas: 4
  burst_replicas: 4
  burst_window_sec: 900  # 15min
  kv_warmup_on_start: true
  prewarm_schedule: 
    - cron: "0 13 * * 1-5"  # market open preheat
      replicas: 6
```
This keeps baseline predictable and gives controlled burst. We should not recommend +100% burst because KV warmup takes time.

noah (Infra): Also callout: Private deployment requires KMS integration test; preheat can fail if key permissions missing. Add KMS checklist to runbook.

emma (AE): Procurement also wants amortized token price if we use quantized model vs FP16. Any quick figures?

julia (Solutions): Typical cost delta: quantized variant reduces GPU-hours ~2.2–2.8x depending on throughput. For quoting, use 2.5x reduction as conservative. We'll show two line items: reserved (baseline) + burst credit bucket per month.

mike (Sales Eng): Can we give a sample cost table? They need it today for CFO sync.

julia (Solutions): I'll put sample numbers into the deck, but we need exact perf numbers. rohan — can you run the microbench on Skyline's model family (they provided model name) with 8k and 18k prompt lengths? If not today, we give conservative engineering estimate.

rohan (SRE): I can run a quick profiler tomorrow AM. For now, conservative capacity rec: reserve 6 GPUs (quantized) with 4 baseline and 2 guaranteed burst slots, plus 100k token burst credits/month. That should cover sustained window and 2x spike headroom.

emma (AE): Okay. Action items: (1) rohan run perf bench on provided model for 8k/18k by 15:00 UTC tomorrow; (2) julia produce cost vs quantized/FP16 table + ops runbook with KMS checklist; (3) noah list lead times and any infra constraints for Private deploy; (4) mike assemble procurement-facing price summary.

mike (Sales Eng): Will do. Also, flagging one enterprise blocker: Skyline's legal wants SLA >99.95 for market hours only (13:00–14:30 PT). We need to ensure reserved placement and AZ spread.

noah (Infra): We can do AZ spread within customer's VPC if they want Private, but that changes placement options and may reduce burst capacity. Call it out in handoff.

rohan (SRE): One last note — fallback model plan: configure automatic degrade to a smaller quantized model if queue depth > 250 for >60s. That keeps tail latencies bounded.

emma (AE): Perfect. I'll update Skyline and ping them for confirmation on Private vs Dedicated tomorrow. Thanks all :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Reminder — security questionnaire 3 of 7 outstanding (KMS, encryption in transit, vendor attestations).

mike (Sales Eng): I'll nudge procurement/legal to clear the KMS permission items today.

emma (AE): Closing thread — we'll reconvene after rohan's bench.
